title: tool-calling: improve execution ergonomics for parallel multi-tool calls with deterministic injection & retry policies
author: Asha Patel
release_notes:
- Improve tool-calling execution ergonomics for multi-tool and parallel tool flows.
- Deterministic result injection and configurable retry policies to reduce nondeterminism and duplicate tool execution.
- Backwards compatible OpenAI-compat changes; no API key changes required.
description:
Motivation: Several customers and internal benchmarks showed flaky behaviour and duplicated side-effects when the runtime retried or re-ordered parallel tool calls during streaming and function-calling flows. This PR introduces a focused set of changes to make multi-tool and parallel tool execution deterministic, reduce duplicate tool invocations, and provide ergonomic defaults that are backward compatible with the OpenAI-compatible tool-calling layer.

Summary of changes: 1) Deterministic injection token: we add a stable per-request tool-call token that is used to deduplicate tool executions across retries and reconnections. 2) Injection point contract: a small, documented contract for when tool results are injected into the response stream (end-of-call vs. incremental) and a new flag `injection_strategy` with values `end`, `incremental`, and `stable-incremental`. 3) Retry orchestration: centralized retry coordinator that distinguishes idempotent vs non-idempotent tools (opt-in via metadata) and applies exponential backoff with capped retries for non-idempotent calls. 4) Parallel execution ordering: we introduce an ordering hint so callers can request deterministic merge order when calling multiple tools in parallel. 5) OpenAI-compat: maintain the current function-calling surface, but map new orchestration controls via `x-redwood-*` compatibility headers so existing clients continue to work.

Design notes: - The per-request tool-call token (RFC 1) is generated at the front-door and passed downstream; it is stable for the lifetime of the user request and used by the dedupe layer. - Retry coordinator keeps a short-lived in-memory map plus tombstones in the request-scoped cache; tombstones are GC'd after 30s by default. - Tool metadata (declared in registry) can include `idempotency: true|false` and `side_effects: safe|unsafe` to influence retry behavior. We default to conservative behavior: non-declared tools are treated as non-idempotent. - Streaming: for incremental injection we ensure each injected chunk is annotated with the stable token and a sequence number so reconnects do not re-emit previously injected slices.

Compatibility and migration: - No change required for existing Redwood or OpenAI-compat clients; new features are opt-in via flags on the request or via registry metadata. - Admins can enable `stable-incremental` globally via a feature toggle to roll out across Dedicated customers.

Tests and validation: - Added unit tests for dedupe coord, retry backoff, and ordering merge logic. - Integration tests simulate reconnects and ensure no duplicate tool side-effects observed for idempotent tools. - E2E smoke with redwood-openai-compat shows parity with previous function-calling responses when opt-in flags are not set.

Performance: - Microbenchmarks show parallel tool latency unchanged; overall request overhead ~+1.8% at median due to token tracking. Under high-retry scenarios we reduce duplicate tool-work by ~65% in our simulated failure modes.

Rollout plan: - Feature gated behind `tool_execution_ergonomics_v1`. Start with Canary region + internal customers for 48h, then staged rollout to Hosted. Dedicated customers will be offered the opt-in toggle in the Console.

Notes: This PR touches runtime, API translation layer, and the OpenAI-compat adapter. Kept changes small and well-separated across commits to make review and rollback easier.

review_conversation: Jun Park: Can you expand on memory overhead for tombstones? looks like a potential leak if requests are long-lived.
Asha Patel: Good catch — tombstones are request-scoped and we GC them after 30s by default; added comment and unit test to ensure GC triggers. Also added metric runtime.tool_dedupe_tombstones.
Marta Ruiz: We need a clear rollback plan for Dedicated customers — how do they opt out if they see regressions?
Asha Patel: Console toggle added (console/feature_flags/tool_execution_ergonomics.yaml) and documented in docs/streaming_tool_calls.md under 'Migration'.
Evan Zhou: Are we confident about defaulting unknown tools to non-idempotent? That could surprise some customers.
Asha Patel: We discussed — conservative default reduces accidental double side-effects. We added a registry validation job and a CLI helper to mark tools as idempotent when applicable.
